claims.statement: This how-to spans FPT/GHEC/GHES and separates repository, environment and organization secret storage and usage.

Repository-secret creation needs collaborator authority for personal repositories. Organization repositories require write on FPT/GHEC/GHES>=3.19 and admin on earlier GHES; the UI sequence creates a named value and lists accessible inherited secrets.
The CLI can set a repository secret interactively or from a file and list names; these examples do not authorize a credential write or prove existing values.
Environment-secret creation needs personal repository ownership or organization repository admin access; navigate the selected environment and create the secret there.
CLI --env selects the named environment for setting/listing secrets; a successful repository-level listing is not environment-scope evidence.
Organization access can be constrained to repositories; FPT Free private repositories cannot access organization secrets. Organization owners or supported secret-management roles control creation.
Organization-secret UI creation requires an explicit repository access policy; distinct tabs depend on the acting role, not universal permission.
Managing organization secrets via CLI needs admin:org beyond default repo/read:org scopes; the example is not authority to broaden a current token.
CLI organization-secret defaults target private repositories; all or selected visibility flags deliberately change that scope and require owner review.
Review the organization secret access policy and repository permissions before updates; displayed navigation is not proof of actual policy enforcement.
Fork-triggered workflows receive no secrets except GITHUB_TOKEN; reusable workflows do not automatically inherit secrets, and Dependabot-triggered workflows do not receive these Actions secrets.
OIDC can replace supported long-lived cloud secrets; mask other sensitive data before emitting logs and do not assume transformation redaction.
Pass secrets through explicit action inputs or environment variables; placeholder workflow syntax is not acceptance of the action or its credential handling.
Secrets cannot be directly referenced in if conditions; job environment variables can support step-level conditions, but actual access still requires review.
An unset referenced secret evaluates to an empty string; this is missing data, not evidence of a healthy authentication flow.
Avoid passing secrets on command lines because process listings/logs can expose arguments; prefer supported environment or stdin transport, and quote unavoidable arguments.
Bash, PowerShell and Cmd examples illustrate shell-specific quoting of environment values; quoting does not remove process-argument exposure.
For values over48KB the guide illustrates encrypted repository files with the decryption passphrase stored as a secret; plaintext from this workaround is not automatically redacted.
The GPG AES256 procedure is an encryption example; commit only encrypted material and avoid disclosing plaintext or passphrase. It grants no blanket publication permission.
The decryption script puts a passphrase in argv; its example must retain the earlier command-argument exposure caveat rather than be copied as a certified production implementation.
chmod/add/push commands illustrate preparing the decryption script and are not execution instructions for this review.
The example decrypts into runner storage and prints plaintext only for demonstration; remove the printing step for production and preserve the no-redaction caveat.
Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding, not encryption; decoded secrets need the same access/log protections. On Windows the guide recommends Bash; other shells may need different commands.
Platform-specific Base64 commands and CLI file-input secret creation are examples; the48KB limit still applies.
The decoding workflow creates a certificate file and demonstrates inspection; it is not blanket permission to print decoded sensitive data.
The secrets-reference navigation link supplies follow-up context, not automatic review credit for another article.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
